source_text:
Ἐρρῶσθαι ὑμᾶς εὐχόμεθα, ἀδελφοί, στοιχοῦντας τῷ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον λόγῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, μεθ̓ οὗ δόξα τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι, ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ τῇ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκλεκτῶν, καθὼς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὁ μακάριος Πολύκαρπος, οὗ γένοιτο ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὰ ἴχνη εὑρεθῆναι ἡμᾶς.
Ταῦτα μετεγράψατο μὲν Γάϊος ἐκ τῶν Εἰρηναίου, μαθητοῦ τοῦ Πολυκάρπου, ὃς καὶ συνεπολιτεύσατο τῷ Εἰρηναίῳ. ἐγὼ δὲ Σωκράτης ἐν Κορίνθῳ ἐκ τῶν Γαΐου ἀντιγράφων ἔγραψα. ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων.
Ἐγὼ δὲ πάλιν Πιόνιος ἐκ τοῦ προγεγραμμένου ἔγραψα ἀναζητήσας αὐτά, κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν φανερώσαντός μοι τοῦ μακαρίου Πολυκάρπου, καθὼς δηλώσω ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς, συναγαγὼν αὐτὰ ἤδη σχεδὸν ἐκ τοῦ χρόνου κεκμηκότα, ἵνα κἀμὲ συναγάγῃ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς μετὰ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν οὐράνιον βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα σὺν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Farewell, transmission notes, and final doxology
orientation: The church of Smyrna closes its letter with a prayer for the readers, then three copyists record how the text was transmitted, ending with a doxology.
pass_a_gloss: To be strong you [we] pray, brothers, walking in the according to the gospel word of Jesus Christ, with whom glory [be] to the God and Father and Holy Spirit, for the salvation of the holy elect, just as bore witness the blessed Polycarp, of whom may it be in the kingdom of Jesus Christ at the footsteps to be found [for] us. These things copied out Gaius from the [writings] of Irenaeus, disciple of Polycarp, who also lived as a citizen with Irenaeus. I however Socrates in Corinth from the copies of Gaius wrote. The grace [be] with all. I however again Pionius from the previously written [text] wrote, having searched out these things, according to a revelation [of] the blessed Polycarp having shown [them] to me, just as I will show in the following, having gathered these things already nearly from time having grown weary, in order that also me may gather the Lord Jesus Christ with his elect into his heavenly kingdom, to whom [be] the glory with the Father and Holy Spirit to the ages of the ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: lived as a citizen with, shared civic life with
having searched out, having sought out

choices.english: We pray that you may be strong
choices.why: The infinitive with εὔχομαι expresses the content of the prayer; 'be strong' keeps the literal sense of ῥώννυμι rather than the conventional letter-closing 'farewell'

choices.term: στοιχοῦντας τῷ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον λόγῳ
choices.english: walking in the word of the gospel
choices.why: The participle modifies 'you' and στοιχέω means walking in line or following a rule; the word order 'the according to the gospel word' is compressed to natural English
rejected: keeping step with the word according to the gospel

choices.term: οὗ γένοιτο ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὰ ἴχνη εὑρεθῆναι ἡμᾶς
choices.english: May we be found at his footsteps in the kingdom of Jesus Christ
choices.why: The optative γένοιτο expresses a wish; 'at his footsteps' keeps the spatial metaphor of πρὸς τὰ ἴχνη
rejected: may it happen that we are found in the footsteps
would that we might be found following his tracks

choices.why: The compound verb means living as a fellow citizen; this keeps the civic metaphor rather than flattening it to 'associated with'

choices.term: ἤδη σχεδὸν ἐκ τοῦ χρόνου κεκμηκότα
choices.english: already nearly worn out by time
choices.why: The perfect participle κεκμηκότα describes the texts as exhausted or decayed; 'worn out by time' captures the physical deterioration of the manuscripts

choices.term: ἵνα κἀμὲ συναγάγῃ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς
choices.english: so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me
choices.why: The purpose clause with ἵνα and the aorist subjunctive expresses Pionius's hope; 'gather' keeps the verb συνάγω, which echoes his own gathering of the text
rejected: that the Lord Jesus Christ may also receive me
so that the Lord Jesus Christ might also collect me

pass_b_english: We pray that you may be strong, brothers and sisters, as you walk according to the word of the gospel of Jesus Christ. With him be glory to God the Father and the Holy Spirit, for the salvation of the holy elect, just as the blessed Polycarp martyred. May we be found following in his footsteps in the kingdom of Jesus Christ.

Gaius transcribed these things from the writings of Irenaeus, a disciple of Polycarp, and Gaius shared citizenship with Irenaeus. I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius. (Some manuscripts read Isocrates.) Grace be with you all.

And I, Pionius, wrote them again from the previously written copy, having searched them out, because the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me in a revelation, as I will make clear in what follows. I gathered them together when they were already nearly worn out by time, so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me with his elect into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: because the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me by a revelation
problems.source_quote: κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν φανερώσαντός μοι τοῦ μακαρίου Πολυκάρπου
problems.why: φανερώσαντός is 'having revealed/made manifest', but 'by a revelation' is redundant with 'revealed'; better 'in a revelation'.
problems.fix: the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me in a revelation

problems.why: πρὸς τὰ ἴχνη means 'to/into his tracks/footsteps' in sense of following; 'at his footsteps' is slightly off.
Glossary requires 'martyr' not 'bore his martyrdom'; ἐμαρτύρησεν means 'bore witness/martyred'.
problems.fix: just as the blessed Polycarp martyred
problems.ruling: ἐμαρτύρησεν means 'bore witness'; 'bore his martyrdom' adds 'his' and changes sense to martyrdom event.

edits.old: because the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me by a revelation
edits.new: because the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me in a revelation

edits.old: just as the blessed Polycarp bore his martyrdom
edits.new: just as the blessed Polycarp martyred

problems.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth
problems.why: Same copyist's name rendered differently across sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one form of the name.

problems.quote: just as the blessed Polycarp martyred
problems.why: Verb 'martyred' used intransitively is not natural English.
problems.fix: Render: 'just as the blessed Polycarp was martyred.'

edits.old: just as the blessed Polycarp martyred.
edits.new: just as the blessed Polycarp was martyred.

edits.old: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth
edits.new: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth

fixed: The name Socrates is already consistent in the English; no change needed.
Changed 'martyred' to 'was martyred' to make the verb natural English.

problems.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius.
problems.why: One copy chain names 'Socrates,' the other 'Isocrates' for the same role; reader cannot tell if these are the same person or different.
problems.fix: Note the variant reading or standardize the name with a footnote.

problems.why: 'Shared citizenship' is an odd phrase; the Greek likely means 'was a fellow citizen' (from the same city), not a political status.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'Gaius was a fellow citizen of Irenaeus.'

edits.new: Gaius was a fellow citizen of Irenaeus.

edits.old: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius.
edits.new: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius. (Some manuscripts read Isocrates.)

fixed: The glossary problem about Socrates/Isocrates is addressed with a parenthetical note in the English.
The unreadable phrase about Gaius's citizenship is corrected to 'fellow citizen'.

problems.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth
problems.why: Section 22 says 'Socrates' then notes manuscripts read 'Isocrates'; epilogus_alius uses 'Isocrates' without note.
problems.fix: Pick one name and note the variant once, or use the same form throughout.

problems.why: Parenthetical manuscript note interrupts the narrative voice; reads like an editor's intrusion in the text.
problems.fix: Move to a footnote or preface rather than inline in the text.

edits.old: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius. (Some manuscripts read Isocrates.)
edits.new: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius.

fixed: The parenthetical manuscript note was removed from the narrative, leaving the name Socrates as in the source. The variant Isocrates is not part of the source text and should be handled outside the translation.

last_rejected.quote: and he shared citizenship with Irenaeus
last_rejected.why: συνεπολιτεύσατο means 'lived with/shared life with', not 'shared citizenship'
last_rejected.ruling: συνεπολιτεύσατο contains πολιτεύω, 'live as citizen'; 'shared citizenship' is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: just as the blessed Polycarp martyred
last_rejected.why: ἐμαρτύρησεν is aorist of μαρτυρέω, 'bore witness/martyred'; but 'martyred' as intransitive verb is awkward and unclear
last_rejected.fix: just as the blessed Polycarp bore witness
last_rejected.ruling: ἐμαρτύρησεν can mean 'bore witness' or 'was martyred'; 'martyred' is acceptable for Polycarp's death.

last_rejected.quote: because the blessed Polycarp revealed them to me in a revelation
last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν φανερώσαντός μοι τοῦ μακαρίου Πολυκάρπου
last_rejected.why: κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν = 'by a revelation', not 'because'; φανερώσαντος = 'having revealed/made manifest', causal misrendering
last_rejected.fix: the blessed Polycarp having revealed them to me by a revelation
last_rejected.ruling: κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν can mean 'according to a revelation'; 'because' paraphrases the causal sense adequately.

last_rejected.quote: as I will make clear in what follows
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter admits the translation is correct; no error exists.

last_rejected.quote: I gathered them together when they were already nearly worn out by time
last_rejected.source_quote: συναγαγὼν αὐτὰ ἤδη σχεδὸν ἐκ τοῦ χρόνου κεκμηκότα
last_rejected.why: συναγαγὼν is aorist participle, 'having gathered'; main verb is ἔγραψα. 'I gathered' makes it coordinate rather than subordinate
last_rejected.fix: having gathered them together when they were already nearly worn out by time
last_rejected.ruling: συναγαγὼν as 'I gathered' is acceptable English rendering of aorist participle; not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα κἀμὲ συναγάγῃ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς
last_rejected.why: κἀμὲ = 'me also', not 'also gather me'; the 'also' applies to the object, not the verb
last_rejected.fix: so that the Lord Jesus Christ may gather me also
last_rejected.ruling: κἀμὲ = 'me also'; 'may also gather me' preserves the 'also' with the object adequately in English.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening prayer by making the subject of walking explicit, replaced the vague 'in his tracks' with 'following in his footsteps,' and clarified that Gaius, not Irenaeus, shared citizenship with Irenaeus.
